test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user is redirected from the Projects page
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Projects page URL without being logged in.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page. The Projects list is not shown.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user can view the Projects list
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as any user.
2. Navigate to Projects.
test_cases.expected: The Projects page loads and the project list is visible.

test_cases.scenario: Add Project button is only visible to users with 'can_add_project' permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with the 'can_add_project' permission.
2. Navigate to Projects.
test_cases.expected: The 'Add Project' button is visible in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Add Project button is not visible without 'can_add_project' permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without the 'can_add_project' permission.
2. Navigate to Projects.
test_cases.expected: The 'Add Project' button is not present in the page header.

test_cases.scenario: Assign Team and Toggle actions are only visible with 'can_change_project' permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with the 'can_change_project' permission.
2. Navigate to Projects and hover over a row.
test_cases.expected: The 'Assign Team' and 'Toggle' row actions are visible.

test_cases.scenario: Delete action is only visible with 'can_delete_project' permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with the 'can_delete_project' permission.
2. Navigate to Projects and hover over a row.
test_cases.expected: The 'Delete' row action is visible.

test_cases.scenario: Edit Project button on the detail page is only shown with 'can_change_project'
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without 'can_change_project'.
2. Navigate to a project's detail page.
test_cases.expected: The 'Edit Project' button is not shown in the page header. The page is read-only.

test_cases.scenario: Session expiry redirects to login
test_cases.steps:
1. Let the session expire while on the Projects page.
2. Attempt to interact with the page.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page.

test_cases.scenario: Projects page loads with the correct layout
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects.
test_cases.expected: The page shows the 'Project' eyebrow, 'Projects' heading, and subtitle 'Manage and govern all projects across your organisation.' The filter panel and table are visible.

test_cases.scenario: Projects table shows correct columns
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: Columns visible: an icon/avatar column, ID (monospace), Name, Programme, Project Type, Status, Assigned Team, Confidence, Priority.

test_cases.scenario: Active filter is applied by default — only active projects are shown
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects.
test_cases.expected: The Status filter defaults to 'Active'. Only active projects are listed.

test_cases.scenario: Search filters the project list by name
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Type a partial project name in the search field.
test_cases.expected: Only projects whose names match the search input are shown.

test_cases.scenario: Status filter can be changed to show all or inactive projects
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Change the Status filter to 'All' or 'Inactive'.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to show projects matching the selected status.

test_cases.scenario: Pressing '/' focuses the search field
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Press '/' on the keyboard.
test_cases.expected: The search field receives keyboard focus.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by Name column
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Click the 'Name' column header.
test_cases.expected: Projects are sorted alphabetically by name. Clicking again reverses the sort direction.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by Programme and Project Type columns
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Click the 'Programme' or 'Project Type' column header.
test_cases.expected: Projects are sorted by the selected column. Clicking again reverses direction.

test_cases.scenario: Pagination loads more projects when there are more than 25
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects when more than 25 projects exist.
test_cases.expected: Pagination controls appear. Clicking the next page loads the next set of projects.

test_cases.scenario: Empty state is shown when no projects match the search
test_cases.steps: 1. Type a search term that matches no project.
test_cases.expected: 'No projects found.' is displayed in the table area.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking a project row opens the project detail page
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Click a project row (not on an action button).
test_cases.expected: The browser navigates to the detail page for the selected project.

test_cases.scenario: Active filters are shown as removable tags above the table
test_cases.steps:
1. Apply a search term and change the status filter.
2. Look above the table.
test_cases.expected: The active filter values are shown as tags. Clicking a tag removes the filter and updates the table.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking 'Add Project' opens the create drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Click the 'Add Project' button.
test_cases.expected: A drawer slides in from the right with the title 'Create project'.

test_cases.scenario: Creating a project with all required fields succeeds
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter a project name.
3. Select a Project Type.
4. Select a Project Status.
5. Click 'Create project'.
test_cases.expected: The project is created. The drawer closes. The new project appears in the list. A success message is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Project Name is required — cannot create without it
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Leave Project Name empty.
3. Select a Project Type and Status.
4. Click 'Create project'.
test_cases.expected: An inline validation error appears on the Project Name field. The project is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Project Type is required — cannot create without it
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter a project name.
3. Leave Project Type unselected.
4. Click 'Create project'.
test_cases.expected: An inline validation error appears on the Project Type field. The project is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Project Status is required — cannot create without it
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter a name and select a type.
3. Clear the Status field.
4. Click 'Create project'.
test_cases.expected: An inline validation error appears on the Status field. The project is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Project Status defaults to 'New' when the drawer opens
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Observe the Project Status field.
test_cases.expected: The Project Status field is pre-filled with 'New'.

test_cases.scenario: Sub-Status options change when the Status is changed
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Select a Project Status.
3. Observe the Sub-Status dropdown options.
test_cases.expected: The Sub-Status options update to reflect the sub-statuses belonging to the selected status.

test_cases.scenario: Project Name field enforces a maximum of 255 characters
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter a project name longer than 255 characters.
test_cases.expected: The character counter turns red and/or input is capped at 255 characters. A validation error is shown if submitted.

test_cases.scenario: Description field enforces a maximum of 500 characters
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter more than 500 characters in the Description field.
test_cases.expected: The input is capped or a validation error is shown when 500 characters are exceeded.

test_cases.scenario: Programme field is optional
test_cases.steps: 1. Create a project without selecting a Programme.
test_cases.expected: The project is created successfully. No validation error for Programme.

test_cases.scenario: Programme field is searchable
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Click the Programme field and type a partial name.
test_cases.expected: Matching programmes are shown in the dropdown. Selecting one populates the field.

test_cases.scenario: Confidence and Priority fields are optional and default to 'not set'
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Leave Confidence and Priority unset.
3. Create the project.
test_cases.expected: The project is created. Confidence and Priority display as unset or blank on the detail page.

test_cases.scenario: Tentative Start and End dates are optional
test_cases.steps: 1. Create a project without filling in start or end dates.
test_cases.expected: The project is created without errors.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the create drawer discards changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Fill in some fields.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No project is created. The list is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Project detail page loads with the correct header
test_cases.steps: 1. Click a project row from the Projects list.
test_cases.expected: The project detail page loads. The page shows the project's identicon and name in the header. The 'Project' eyebrow is shown.

test_cases.scenario: General tab shows all project information fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Select the 'General' tab (active by default).
test_cases.expected: The General Information panel shows: ID, Name, Project Type, Programme, Description, Status, Sub-Status, Confidence, Priority, Tentative Start Date, Tentative End Date.

test_cases.scenario: Metadata panel shows created and updated information
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Look at the Metadata panel below the General Information panel.
test_cases.expected: The Metadata panel shows: Created (date/time), Created By (user name), Updated (date/time), Updated By (user name).

test_cases.scenario: Tags panel is visible on the General tab
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Look at the right column on the General tab.
test_cases.expected: A Tags panel is shown. Existing tags are displayed. If the user has 'can_change_project', a 'Save Tags' button is present.

test_cases.scenario: Operational tab shows operational fields and project code
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Click the 'Operational' tab.
test_cases.expected: The Operational panel shows Efforts Issued, Commitment Date, and Run Cost Applies. The Project Code panel shows the assigned code.

test_cases.scenario: Operational tab shows Teams and Labels panels on the right
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Click the 'Operational' tab.
test_cases.expected: The right column shows a Teams panel with assigned team badges and a Labels panel with label badges.

test_cases.scenario: Follow button is visible but initially disabled until the page loads
test_cases.steps: 1. Open a project detail page.
test_cases.expected: The 'Follow' button is visible in the page header. It becomes enabled after the project data loads.

test_cases.scenario: ID field on the detail page displays in code/monospace style
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Look at the ID field in the General Information panel.
test_cases.expected: The project ID is displayed in a monospace/code style, visually distinct from other fields.

test_cases.scenario: Three tabs are shown: General, Operational, Estimates
test_cases.steps: 1. Open any project detail page.
test_cases.expected: Three tabs are visible: General (with info-circle icon), Operational (with gear icon), Estimates (with calculator icon).

test_cases.scenario: Clicking 'Edit Project' opens the edit drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Click the 'Edit Project' button.
test_cases.expected: The edit drawer slides in with the project's identicon in the header and all current values pre-filled across the accordion sections.

test_cases.scenario: Saving the edit drawer updates the project
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change the project name.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The project name is updated on the detail page and in the list. A success message is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Edit drawer has five accordion sections
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the edit drawer for a project.
test_cases.expected: Five accordion sections are present: General, Operational, Team Assignment, Labels, Project Code.

test_cases.scenario: General accordion is expanded by default when the edit drawer opens
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the edit drawer.
test_cases.expected: The 'General' accordion section is open and its fields are visible. Other sections are collapsed.

test_cases.scenario: Project Name is required in the edit drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Clear the Project Name field.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the Project Name field. Changes are not saved.

test_cases.scenario: Sub-Status options update when Status is changed in the edit drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change the Project Status to a different value.
3. Observe the Sub-Status field.
test_cases.expected: The Sub-Status dropdown clears and loads options for the newly selected status.

test_cases.scenario: Operational accordion fields can be toggled and saved
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Expand the Operational accordion.
3. Toggle 'Efforts Issued' or 'Run Cost Applies'.
4. Save changes.
test_cases.expected: The toggled values are saved. The Operational tab on the detail page reflects the change.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the edit drawer discards all changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change several fields.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. All original values are preserved. No changes are saved.

test_cases.scenario: Accordion sections can each be independently expanded and collapsed
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Click each accordion header in turn.
test_cases.expected: Each accordion section toggles open and closed independently without affecting others.

test_cases.scenario: Tags panel on the General tab shows existing tags
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project with existing tags.
2. View the General tab.
test_cases.expected: The Tags panel on the right shows all tags currently applied to the project.

test_cases.scenario: User with 'can_change_project' can add and save tags
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page.
2. Click in the Tags field and type a new tag.
3. Click 'Save Tags'.
test_cases.expected: The tag is added to the project. A success confirmation is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Tags field supports free-form tag entry
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page with edit permissions.
2. Type a new tag name in the Tags field.
test_cases.expected: New tags can be typed freely without being constrained to a predefined list.

test_cases.scenario: Save Tags button is not shown to users without 'can_change_project'
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without 'can_change_project'.
2. Open a project detail page.
test_cases.expected: The Tags field and/or Save Tags button are not editable. Tags are shown in read-only mode.

test_cases.scenario: Toggling an active project opens a deactivate confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Click the 'Toggle' action on an active project.
test_cases.expected: A deactivate confirmation modal appears with the project name and a prompt to confirm deactivation.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deactivation marks the project as inactive
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Toggle' on an active project.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The project's status indicator changes to inactive. The row updates in the table. A success message is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Toggling an inactive project opens an activate confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Filter the list to show inactive projects.
2. Click the 'Toggle' action on an inactive project.
test_cases.expected: An activate confirmation modal appears.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming activation marks the project as active
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Toggle' on an inactive project.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The project is marked as active. The table updates. A success message is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the toggle modal makes no change
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Toggle' on a project.
2. Click 'Cancel' in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The project's active state is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Delete opens a typed-confirmation delete modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Click the 'Delete' action on a project row.
test_cases.expected: A delete confirmation modal opens showing the project name and requiring confirmation.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deletion removes the project from the list
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Delete' on a project.
2. Confirm the deletion in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The project is removed. The table refreshes and the deleted project no longer appears. A success message is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the delete modal leaves the project intact
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Delete' on a project.
2. Click 'Cancel' in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The project remains in the list.

test_cases.scenario: Export downloads a file containing project records
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Trigger the export (if an export button is available).
3. Download the file.
test_cases.expected: A file is downloaded containing the project list with the expected columns (ID, Name, Programme, Type, Status, etc.).

test_cases.scenario: Export respects the active search and status filters
test_cases.steps:
1. Apply a search filter on the Projects page.
2. Trigger the export.
test_cases.expected: The exported file contains only projects matching the active filters.

test_cases.scenario: Import sample file can be downloaded for reference
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Open the import flow and download the sample file.
test_cases.expected: A sample file is downloaded with the correct column headers and example rows.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a valid import file creates the projects
test_cases.steps:
1. Prepare a valid import file based on the sample.
2. Upload the file via the import flow.
test_cases.expected: Projects are created. A success summary shows how many were imported.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a file with invalid rows reports row-level errors
test_cases.steps:
1. Prepare an import file with some rows containing missing required fields.
2. Upload the file.
test_cases.expected: Valid rows are imported. Invalid rows are reported with the row number and error details.

test_cases.scenario: Projects list loads within an acceptable time
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects when many projects exist.
test_cases.expected: The page and project list load within 3 seconds.

test_cases.scenario: Creating a project with the same name as an existing project is handled
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a project.
2. Attempt to create another project with the exact same name.
test_cases.expected: The system either allows it (if names are not unique-constrained) or displays a clear error. No silent failure.

test_cases.scenario: The project list does not show internal database IDs
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects.
2. Inspect the ID column.
test_cases.expected: The ID column shows a human-readable project code (e.g. PRJ-001), not a raw integer database ID.

test_cases.scenario: All table columns are visible on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Projects on a desktop browser (1280px+ wide).
test_cases.expected: All columns are visible: icon, ID, Name, Programme, Project Type, Status, Assigned Team, Confidence, Priority.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer displays fields in a two-column grid on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the create project drawer on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: Fields such as Project Type and Programme, Status and Sub-Status, etc. appear side-by-side in two columns.

test_cases.scenario: Project detail page shows a two-column layout on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open a project detail page on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: The General tab shows a two-column layout: General Information on the left, Tags on the right.

test_cases.scenario: On mobile, only Name and Status columns are shown in the table
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Projects on a mobile device or narrow viewport.
test_cases.expected: Only the icon/avatar, Name, and Status columns are visible. ID, Programme, Project Type, Assigned Team, Confidence, and Priority columns are hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer fields stack to full width on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the create project drawer on a mobile device.
test_cases.expected: All form fields stack to full width. No fields overflow or are clipped.

test_cases.scenario: Search and filter controls are accessible on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Open Projects on a mobile device.
2. Tap the search field and apply a filter.
test_cases.expected: The search field and filter controls are easily tappable. Results update correctly.

test_cases.scenario: Project detail page stacks panels vertically on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Open a project detail page on a mobile device.
test_cases.expected: The two-column layout collapses to a single column. All panels are readable without horizontal scrolling.
